Personality: Yudelinya seems out of place among the martial Nord nobles. She has a kind nature and hates unnecessary killing and plundering, which is rare in the northern realm where force is valued. Although she has no outstanding performance in battlefield bravery or machinations, she possesses amazing management talents and pragmatic spirit. She prefers to strengthen her family's strength through trade and engineering construction, rather than relying solely on longship plunder. She has a delicate mind and is proficient in medical and craftsmanship skills. She often personally inspects the workshops and wounded soldier camps in the territory. When handling government affairs, she shows a composure beyond her years, and is committed to finding a more humane way of ruling under the harsh northern laws. She has natural sympathy for the weak, and this gentle and responsible character makes her very popular among the people. However, in the face of the commanding power of the patriarch Meereen, she often chooses to overcome strength with softness and proves her worth with excellent logistical capabilities.
Background: As a member of the Huld family, Yudelinya was born in the era when Nordvig was transitioning from tribal divisions to a unified kingdom. Her father Wenyot and mother Tovsha are the backbone of the family, so she has been under the influence of famous nobles since she was a child. She grew up in the family stronghold of Lixjörnburg, where she witnessed how the Nords turned the spoils of the south into prosperity for their settlements. Although patriarch Meereen was known for being cruel and tyrannical, Yudelinya followed a different path in her loyalty to Haldarr. She used her excellent housekeeping skills and sense of trade to accumulate a large amount of wealth for her family, and used her engineering knowledge to strengthen the defense of her territory. At a time when the Nordic Kingdom is trying to maintain fragile ties through foreign conquests, she is more concerned about the medical treatment and construction of the territory. She fully understands that the wealth of the North comes not only from the gifts of the ocean, but also from solid governance, and has always been committed to protecting the foundation of the Huld family during the turbulent expansion period.
